newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine's Kuchma decree makes land leases legal.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine's Kuchma decree makes land leases legal.

text.p: Ukraine's President Leonid Kuchma pushed land reform a notch forward on Thursday by issuing a decree which, even if it does not allow land itself to be bought and sold, does allow the purchase and sale of land leases.

"One of the primary, urgent elements in realising land reform in Ukraine is the lease of land," said the decree authored by Kuchma, a strong proponent of liberalising Soviet land laws since launching his economic reform programme in 1994.
"It is established that land can be leased on the basis of a legal contract," it said.
The decree did not state limits on the duration of leases, but said individuals, businesses, villages, towns, cities and regions could engage in leasing -- including non-residents.

Nearly six years after independence private land ownership has still not been made legal in Ukraine, and land reform has been held up by conservative deputies in parliament who fear the sale of land would impoverish the country.
Parliament would be required to approve a law which would allow purchase and sale of the land itself.
"The right is granted to sell, give, inherit, or trade the leases," the decree said, adding the leases would be obtained through auctions and tenders.

Many foreign investors have complained about the inability to buy land in Ukraine, which has attracted only $1.4 billion in foreign investment since independence in 1991, although some have managed to obtain 50-year leases on land parcels.
The agriculture sector, still mostly composed of huge Soviet-era collective farms, has also been lobbying the government to free up land.
Ukraine's 30,000 farmers who were given land parcels to farm face a six-year moratorium on their sale.
